answer: A raven remembers who fed it, so testimony must trace to distinct providers. Each identity needs two holders outside its own wharf to vouch for it, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n separate vouchers rather than one crew. Every claim is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A falcon audit replays a random claim each epoch; an unconfirmed claim forfeits its bond to the pool and cannot be resold or re-pooled across heads.
